pr.title: coverage: Completely overhaul counter assignment, using node-flow graphs
pr.description:
The existing code for choosing where to put physical counter-increments gets the job done, but is very ad-hoc and hard to modify without introducing tricky regressions.

This PR replaces all of that with a more principled approach, based on the algorithm described in "Optimal measurement points for program frequency counts" (Knuth & Stevenson, 1973).

---

We start by ensuring that our graph has “balanced flow”, i.e. each node's flow (execution count) is equal to the sum of all its in-edge flows, and equal to the sum of all its out-edge flows. That isn't naturally true of control-flow graphs, so we introduce a wrapper type `BalancedFlowGraph` to fix that by introducing synthetic nodes and edges as needed.

Once our graph has balanced flow, the next step is to create another view of that graph in which each node's successors have all been merged into one “supernode”. Consequently, each node's out-edges can be coalesced into a single out-edge to one of those supernodes. Because of the balanced-flow property, the flow of that coalesced edge is equal to the flow of the original node.

Having expressed all of our node flows as edge flows, we can then analyze node flows using techniques for analyzing edge flows. We incrementally build a spanning tree over the merged supernodes, such that each new edge in the spanning tree represents a node whose flow can be computed from that of other nodes.

When this is done, we end up with a list of “counter terms” for each node, describing which nodes need physical counters, and how the remaining nodes can have their flow calculated by adding and subtracting those physical counters.

---

The re-blessed coverage tests show that this results in modest or major improvements for our test programs. Some tests need fewer physical counters, some tests need fewer expression nodes for the same number of physical counters, and some tests show striking reductions in both.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason:
The PR (rust-lang/rust#135481) is a counter-assignment optimization/cleanup, not a semantic bug fix. Its own description and the supplied analysis state that the old ready-first edge-capable assignment and the new balanced-flow/supernode spanning-tree node-flow assignment both compute the same BCB execution counts; the change reduces the number and shape of physical counters and expression terms. The re-blessed `.coverage`/`.cov-map` diffs show changed counter/expression placement (e.g. `+c0+c1` becoming `+c1-c0`) rather than an old-vs-new value mismatch that can be attributed to a wrong historical transformation. Modeling the two counter-allocation policies over a concrete CFG would therefore produce mathematically equivalent counts, so any forced difference would have to invent an unrelated return-value change, which the task forbids.

The one genuine correctness fix in the patch (`DenseBitSet::union_not` calling `clear_excess_bits` after `a | !b`) belongs to `rustc_index`, not to the `InstrumentCoverage` pass listed in `passIds`, and it is a new utility rather than the historical counter-assignment transformation under test. It cannot be used to construct a source-grounded InstrumentCoverage counterexample.

Consequently there is no valid historical original/transformed function pair for `InstrumentCoverage` that differs on concrete inputs while remaining faithful to the PR. No `test_program_pair` counterexample can be validated without manufacturing semantics the PR does not contain.

analysis.originalLogic: The pre-PR `InstrumentCoverage` counter assignment used `CountersBuilder` driven by `ReadyFirstTraversal` over the `CoverageGraph`. For each BCB needing coverage, it ensured a node counter and, when `is_out_summable`, also considered out-edge counters. A node with multiple in-edges could get a `NodeSumExpr` by creating counters for all in-edges; an out-edge could get an `EdgeDiffExpr` equal to its source node counter minus its sibling out-edge counters. It preferred making the reloop edge an expression (`find_good_reloop_edge`) instead of assigning it a physical counter. Physical counters could be placed on nodes or edges, and a later `Transcriber` resolved these symbolic site counters, flattened them into positive/negative physical-site lists, and used `sort_and_cancel` to cancel matching terms.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical, superseded optimization policy (not a confirmed bug fix): assign counters ad hoc while traversing the BCB graph in ready-first order, placing physical counters on both BCB nodes and BCB edges; compute node counts as sums of in-edge counters and edge counts as source-node counters minus sibling out-edge counters; choose a reloop out-edge heuristically for an expression; then flatten/cancel the resulting symbolic expression. The PR replaces this with a global Knuth–Stevenson node-flow assignment: add a synthetic sink to impose balanced flow, merge each node's successors into a supernode, build a spanning tree over supernodes, and derive each node's counter expression from physically measured nodes. This is an optimization/cleanup overhaul, not evidence that the old output was semantically wrong.
analysis.inputDomain: `InstrumentCoverage` counter construction for a single MIR body: the coverage-relevant `CoverageGraph` after BCB construction, with dense BCB indices, a start BCB, loop headers/reloop edges, per-BCB `is_out_summable`, and a `bcb_needs_counter` bitset whose domain is the number of BCBs. The two comparison variants should use the same CFG and same set of BCBs needing counters, differing only in the counter-assignment transformation: old edge-capable ready-first site-counter construction versus new balanced-flow/supernode spanning-tree node-counter construction. The new path additionally assumes all underlying nodes are reachable from the start node and appends a synthetic sink at index `graph.num_nodes()`.
analysis.summary: Replaced `InstrumentCoverage`'s ad-hoc ready-first node/edge counter assignment with a balanced-flow graph plus supernode/spanning-tree node-flow algorithm. The optimization reduces physical counters and expression nodes while preserving counter-expression semantics; re-blessed coverage tests reflect changed, generally improved counter placement rather than a proven semantic bug fix.
analysis.trigger: Whenever coverage counters are generated for a function whose coverage graph has branches, loops, return/yield nodes, or inescapable loops. The new transformation runs unconditionally from `CoverageCounters::new`: it builds `BalancedFlowGraph::for_graph(graph, |n| !graph[n].is_out_summable)`, then `MergedNodeFlowGraph::for_balanced_graph`, then `make_node_counters` over an ordered node permutation and transcribes only node counters.
preconditions: All nodes in the underlying graph are reachable from the start node: BalancedFlowGraph documents 'Assumes that all nodes in the underlying graph are reachable from the start node.'

The sink is synthetic and has index equal to the underlying graph's `num_nodes()`; it has synthetic in-edges from terminal nodes, forced sink-edge nodes, and nodes reverse-unreachable from those seeds, plus one synthetic out-edge back to the start node.
`force_sink_edge` is supplied as `|n| !graph[n].is_out_summable`, covering nodes such as returns/yields where out-flow need not equal in-flow.
Every node in the balanced graph must have at least one out-edge, so successor merging can use `reduce(...).expect("each node in a balanced graph must have at least one out-edge")`.
`make_node_counters` must receive exactly one copy of every node; `visit_node` asserts `node has already been visited` if repeated and `finish` asserts no nodes remain unvisited.
The first node in the reversed iteration is the synthetic sink and must not receive a physical counter; the code asserts `nodes[0] == balanced_graph.sink`.
Only supernodes may own spanning-tree edges, and `succ_supernodes` must be canonicalized through `supernodes.find` after freezing the union-find.
pitfalls: Do not run the node-flow algorithm directly on an ordinary CFG without balancing: the design notes that start nodes have no in-edge, return nodes have no out-edge, yield out-flow can be less than in-flow, and inescapable loops break in/out-flow equality.
The sink is not a real measurement point: assigning it a physical counter would be invalid; ordering places it first specifically to exclude it.

Reloop nodes should be preferred for expressions, not physical counters: the code defines a reloop node as having exactly one out-edge whose target dominates the node and notes they are 'typically visited more times than loop-exit nodes'.

Node ordering is only a priority hint: return/yield nodes prefer physical counters, reloop nodes prefer expressions, and otherwise dominating nodes prefer physical counters; changing the order changes which nodes are measured versus derived.

When a spanning-tree edge would create a cycle, the node gets a physical counter and that counter is added to the claiming expressions along the path to its supernode root; if a spantree edge was reversed an odd number of times, the counter term must use `Op::Subtract`, otherwise `Op::Add`.

Do not retain old edge instrumentation assumptions: the PR removes `Site::Edge`, edge counter blocks, and `inject_edge_counter_basic_block`; the remaining FIXME says the Site enum is no longer needed because 'we only instrument nodes and not edges'.

Transcription must still handle fallback safely: if no positive counter terms remain, the code debug-asserts and creates a physical counter for the BCB 'to avoid an ICE' rather than assuming it cannot happen.
`DenseBitSet::union_not` computes `self | !other`; because this can set excess bits in the final word, it must call `clear_excess_bits` afterwards.

Re-blessed `.coverage`/`.cov-map` files are not proof that the old assignments were wrong. For example, the `assert.coverage` line counts change from `while ... 11` to `10` and from `Ok(())`/closing brace `0` to `1`; treat these as changed counter placement/mapping outputs unless a separate semantic test confirms a bug.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused unit tests for each graph layer plus coverage end-to-end checks. For node-flow, use `VecGraph` and the Knuth–Stevenson example with edges `(0,1),(0,3),(1,0),(1,2),(2,1),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4),(4,0)`, visit in order `[3,1,2,0,4]`, and assert the formatted counter expressions `[0]: +c0`, `[1]: +c0 +c2 -c4`, `[2]: +c2`, `[3]: +c3`, `[4]: +c4`. Add union-find tests for singleton roots and transitive unification. Add a `union_not` bitset test over a 100-element domain that verifies all elements except the non-overlapping members of the subtracted set remain, exercising excess final-word bits. Then inspect/re-bless `tests/mir-opt/coverage/*.diff` and `tests/coverage/*.cov-map`/`*.coverage`, checking that derived expressions add/subtract physically measured counters correctly and that the new policy uses fewer or equal physical counters/terms for the same CFG.
